summary: Santa Barbara County fire lookout on Mount Solomon, built 1934 and staffed into 1948 per newspaper clippings; FFLA lists it gone and the summit is now described as antenna-crowned.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists the tower as gone; peakbagging labels the site an LO site, meaning the building has been removed

events.note: Under construction April 1934; about 95 percent complete late June; ready for use by July 15 per clippings. Builder reported inconsistently (federal government or state under federal supervision)
Bard Davison, former county fire patrolman, took charge; family moved up late June 1934
Osborn allidade fire finder installed at the station
Charles Barnes appointed lookout for the season; station cleaned and repainted
Bessie Hampton had staffed it four summers by December 1948; watch about May 15 to November

resolved_conflicts.explanation: April 1934 clipping says the federal government would build the station; a June 1934 clipping says the state built it under federal forest supervision. Not resolved; the story reports both.

A 1934 item gives about 2,000 feet for the station; a 1948 article gives 1,336 feet for the mountain; the peak table gives 1,344 feet for the lookout. The story gives each figure with its source and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Clippings (via Kemnow) give the 1934-1948 history; FFLA gives gone status; the Santa Maria Times feature (undated) gives the antenna-crowned summit. Unresolved: builder (federal vs state) and station height (about 2,000 ft in 1934 vs 1,336/1,344 ft later). No removal date, no removal record and no current access statement found. The FFLA entry 'Solomon' (Tehama/Trinity, no coordinates) is a different record and was not used. Staffing 'unstaffed' is inferred from the gone status. Two WebSearch calls used; no further reads of other sites. Fact-check 2026-10-10: staffing changed from 'unstaffed' (an inference from the gone status, no source states it) to 'unknown'. Dated evidence anchors added from the dated clippings on the Kemnow page; the 1,344 ft lookout elevation is confirmed in the peak table row.
